items.title: Tax and sourcing
items.text: Check each withdrawal's use and invoice, and which channel bars come through

notes: Finally, five things we would like to decide with you. We will discuss them in groups after this session and settle them next month. One, the new-line mix: how much heritage gold, design pieces and light pieces, set region by region because customers differ. Two, pricing rules: which pieces carry a fixed price and which are sold by weight, how often fixed prices are reviewed, and how big a gold move triggers a change. Three, trade-ins: whether every store works to the industry standard, and who provides testing equipment and receipt templates. Four, gold-price risk: every store keeps a ledger of its gold exposure, and we ask whether head office should arrange bank gold leasing and hedging for dealers who choose to join. Five, tax and sourcing: check what each withdrawal of gold is for and the invoice that goes with it. The World Gold Council found that after the tax change gold bars from non-member channels, such as independent gold shops and brand franchise stores, rose by about 13%, while member channels such as banks and brands' own stores were not affected. So which channel our bars come through is worth working out together. None of these has a ready answer. They all need your experience.
